definitions.explanation: One of the Japanese syllabary writing systems, typically used for foreign words and emphasis.

examples.japanese: {片仮名|かたかな}を{覚|おぼ}える。
この{言葉|ことば}は{片仮名|かたかな}で{書|か}きます。
examples.english: This word is written in katakana.

examples.japanese: {外国|がいこく}の{名前|なまえ}は{片仮名|かたかな}で{書|か}きます。
examples.english: Foreign names are written in katakana.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のとき、{平仮名|ひらがな}より{片仮名|かたかな}のほうが{難|むずか}しかった。
examples.english: When I was a child, katakana was harder than hiragana.

notes:
One of the three Japanese writing systems. {片仮名|かたかな} characters are angular, in contrast to the rounded shapes of {平仮名|ひらがな}. Often written as カタカナ in casual contexts.

MAIN USES:
- Foreign loanwords: コーヒー (coffee), テレビ (television)
- Onomatopoeia: ガタガタ, ドキドキ
- Emphasis: similar to italics or bold in English
- Scientific and technical terms: animal/plant names in biology
- Telegrams and older official documents

JAPANESE WRITING SYSTEMS:
- {平仮名|ひらがな}: hiragana — native words, grammar
- {片仮名|かたかな}: katakana — foreign words, emphasis
- {漢字|かんじ}: kanji — Chinese characters

ETYMOLOGY:
{片|かた} means "partial" — {片仮名|かたかな} characters were derived from parts of {漢字|かんじ}. For example, ア comes from {阿|あ}.
